entries.test: Repeated evaluations of contemporaneous ChatGPT on identical and equivalent prompts would establish its variability, reliability, and whether individual examples represent its performance.
entries.note: The proposition links stochastic unreliability to the limited evidential force of single examples.

entries.test: Systematic evaluations of contemporaneous LLMs on factual, commonsense, and causal reasoning tasks would test whether they reliably demonstrate understanding of the world.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give reliability a practical reading in terms of errors and generalization.

entries.test: Public research available by publication showing explanatory discoveries about the world or human mind derived from LLMs would test the assertion that they had taught us nothing.
entries.note: “Ditto for the human mind” carries forward the qualification about explaining why things are as they are. The normalization broadens this to any knowledge about the mind.

entries.test: Comparative studies of LLM mechanisms, human reasoning, and symbolic algorithms on matched tasks would test how often correct LLM outputs involve the same abstractions.
entries.note: The source says a symbolic machine “might use” those abstractions; the normalization changes this to “would use.”

entries.test: Minerva’s published training description and evaluation results on two-digit arithmetic and four-digit multiplication would settle the claim.
entries.note: “Fails altogether” makes a strong empirical assertion about four-digit multiplication.

entries.test: Public controlled studies of Minerva’s dependence on training-example frequency and its transfer to novel multiplication cases would distinguish example matching from a general multiplication procedure.
entries.note: Marcus asserts a preferred causal explanation. The drafter’s “likely” modality does not appear in the quoted wording.

entries.test: Systematic evaluations of contemporaneous LLMs on similar examples, distribution shifts, and attempts to break demonstrated generalizations would test the asserted limits.
entries.note: “A degree of generalization to similar examples” does not assert that generalization occurs only to similar examples. “Can be easily broken” asserts vulnerability rather than a speculative possibility.

entries.test: The cited prompt and response, together with controlled variations and public mechanistic evidence, would test whether its counting and sorting errors arose from similarity matching rather than general procedures.
entries.note: The source explains errors in a particular example; the normalization presents a general explanation of counting and sorting errors.

entries.test: The referenced counting and sorting prompt and ChatGPT response would establish whether a clear, answerable request nevertheless received an incorrect answer.
entries.note: The source addresses one request and its result. The normalization broadens this to failures on clear prompts generally.
The normalization supplies “the job of genuine understanding,” which the sentence does not specify. This broader formulation supplies no shared criterion for genuine understanding.
“A long way from true artificial intelligence” and “even further” supply neither shared endpoints nor a common measure of distance.
